gist: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious after a failed lethal injection execution.
Lawyers claim prison officials botched the execution by failing to insert IV lines correctly.
Tennessee's governor ordered an independent review and halted all executions for the year.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike is unconscious and on a ventilator following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion to preserve evidence, alleging prison officials botched the lethal injection. They state officials used at least seven needles, bending one, while Pike whimpered and cried. An expert suggested the drug pentobarbital entered tissue under her skin rather than her bloodstream due to ruptured veins or blood clots.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions in the state for the year and ordered an independent review. Pike's lawyers had previously warned that her blood-clotting condition and small veins risked causing unnecessary pain.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities have not yet said whether they will attempt to execute Pike again, and her lawyers are seeking to preserve all physical, written, and electronic evidence.

sections.text: Donald Trump is defending US economic performance on the campaign trail, dismissing cost-of-living concerns as a hoax. However, polls show high public discontent with inflation and prices. Consequently, Republican candidates like Byron Donalds in Florida are adapting their messaging to acknowledge that living costs are high, sometimes avoiding mentioning Trump.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: While Trump remains upbeat and blames poor public relations for voter dissatisfaction, his policies and dismissal of economic struggles clash with voter priorities. Candidates must balance loyalty to Trump with addressing the affordability issues that voters care about most.

sections.heading: What happens next

gist: Russian forces have stripped hospitals in occupied Ukraine of vital equipment and supplies.
Patients face severe medical shortages, forced passportisation, and lack of qualified staff.
Extreme conditions have forced medical staff to perform surgeries using phone torches.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Russian forces have stripped hospitals in occupied Ukrainian territories of equipment, medicine, and furniture, redirecting resources to their military. Many experienced medical staff have fled. Patients face severe shortages, with some surgeries performed without anaesthesia or using mobile phone torches for light.

sections.heading: Why it matters

gist: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Chemistry Nobel Prize.
They solved the century-old mystery of life's molecular asymmetry, known as chirality.
Their work allows chemical reactions to produce specific mirror-image molecule forms.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai for solving the mystery of life's asymmetry. Kagan discovered a new way of manipulating chemical reactions in 1986, and Soai developed a reaction in 1995 and 2003 that could produce only the desired version of an organic molecule.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Living organisms exclusively function with one version of mirror-image molecules, a property called chirality. Understanding how to control this is crucial for making effective medicines, as different versions of chiral drug molecules can have entirely different biological effects, such as the toxic versus effective forms seen in thalidomide.

gist: Protesters in Madrid have camped out to protest Spain's worsening housing crisis.
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap general election after housing reforms were rejected.
While protesters blame vulture funds, experts point primarily to a severe housing shortage.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Protesters have pitched hundreds of tents in Madrid's Puerta del Sol square amid widespread anger over surging rental costs. The movement gained momentum following the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap general election after Congress rejected emergency housing legislation.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Housing has become Spaniards' biggest concern as rental costs rose sharply over the past decade. Protesters and the government blame speculative investment funds and tourism, while economic experts suggest the main driver is a severe shortage of new homes compared to growing demand.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Campaigners intend to maintain pressure through upcoming elections and potential strikes. It remains uncertain whether political parties will unite to implement effective solutions to the housing crisis before voters go to the polls.

fivew: Protesters, housing activists, ordinary Spaniards, and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

Following recent protests and the eviction of Maricarmen Abascal, ahead of a snap election next month.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Aerial surveys and tracking studies revealed a 63% decline in occupied chinstrap penguin nests on Zavodovski Island between 2011 and 2025. This loss means the island has lost its title as home to the world's largest penguin colony. While chinstrap numbers crashed, macaroni penguin populations on the same island increased.

sections.heading: Why it matters

stories.title: Chemistry Nobel goes to reactions like those that gave life a hand
stories.standfirst: Altering molecular handedness has implications for the origins of life.

articles.title: Chemistry Nobel goes to reactions like those that gave life a hand
articles.standfirst: Altering molecular handedness has implications for the origins of life.

timeline.text: Chemistry Nobel goes to reactions like those that gave life a hand

gist: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Chemistry Nobel for biased chiral reactions.
Their discoveries explain how chemical reactions can produce excesses of single molecular forms.
This research has practical applications for pharmaceuticals and implications for origin-of-life studies.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering chemical reactions that produce large excesses of one chiral form of a molecule. Kagan showed that a chiral catalyst could drive reactions favoring a single chirality. Soai found reactions where a product acted as a catalyst to boost the same reaction, turning a tiny initial excess into over 99 percent of a single form.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Life relies on molecules with specific handedness, or chirality, and key enzymes fail to work with the wrong form. Finding new ways to catalyze specific chiral forms helps address challenges in origin-of-life research. It also has immense practical utility for producing pharmaceuticals, as wrong chiral forms in drugs can be inactive or harmful.

gist: Women make up a small fraction of new hires in AI roles.
Female tech workers face barriers such as uneven pay and lack of infrastructure.
Companies are scaling back diversity initiatives that previously supported women.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Women accounted for approximately a quarter of new hires in artificial intelligence roles over the past year, and just thirteen percent in executive positions. Meanwhile, women are overrepresented in roles exposed to AI disruption such as customer service. Across all AI occupations, men hold a higher median pay, and women are disproportionately concentrated in low-paying jobs like data annotators.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Advocates warn that this trend could create the greatest gender pay gap in generations. It risks leaving women out of building foundational technology and transforming a participation gap into a power gap.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Companies are scaling back diversity, equity and inclusion programs due to political climates and legal enforcement, leaving fewer institutional initiatives to hire and promote women.

quotes.text: What we’re witnessing is a sort of backsliding

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Eighty-seven-year-old Maricarmen Abascal died in hospital two weeks after being removed on a stretcher from her Madrid home of over seven decades. gist: Pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton has died at the age of 90.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Computer pioneer Margaret Hamilton has died aged 90, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology announced. The Guardian reported she died on 30 September, while Ars Technica noted she died last week. Hamilton learned programming at MIT, worked on weather simulations and air defence projects, and became the first programmer and first woman hired by MIT's Instrumentation Lab for Nasa's Apollo programme. In 2016, President Barack Obama presented her with the nation's highest civilian honour, which the BBC called the Presidential Medal of Honor and other outlets identified as the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Hamilton coined the term software engineering and directed the Apollo onboard flight software development. During the 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing, her software's failsafe mechanisms compensated for computer overloads, averting an abort and allowing the Eagle module to land safely.

sections.text: French finance minister Roland Lescure has invited the UK to rejoin the European Union. sections.text: Actor and writer Reece Shearsmith has released a new book, "Things I Took from the Dark", exploring his lifelong fascination with the macabre. The book serves as a memoir of his early years and a compendium of eerie legends, complete with his own illustrations. It is structured around an imaginary museum featuring famous myths and artefacts that have shaped his career.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Shearsmith's childhood obsession with horror and the supernatural directly inspired his work on successful television series like "The League of Gentlemen", "Psychoville", and "Inside No 9". He believes the enduring appeal of supernatural tales stems from a collective fascination with mortality, offering comfort in the idea that death might not be the end.

gist: Supernatural thriller Below is a six-part series set in a struggling Newfoundland fishing community.

The series stars Josh Hartnett, Charlie Heaton, Mackenzie Davis, and David Wenham.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Netflix has released Below, a six-part supernatural thriller set in the struggling Newfoundland fishing community of Snook's Arm. Created by Jesse McKeown, the series follows local residents, played by Josh Hartnett and Charlie Heaton, as they confront a mysterious iceberg in their harbour. A scientist, played by Mackenzie Davis, discovers the mass is actually a giant frozen mucous membrane. This snot-berg was created by a massive squid, which was released by thawing Arctic permafrost and has begun killing people.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The series attempts to address environmental themes, with fleeting references to warming oceans. However, these climate change elements are largely overshadowed by traditional sea-monster horror tropes, action, and references to classic films like Jaws and The Thing.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Researchers found that watching a "People's Emergency Briefing" film significantly increased viewers' motivation to act on climate and nature breakdown. A survey of 13,000 viewers showed that 93% felt the public is not being fully informed about these crises.

sections.text: Professor Lorraine Whitmarsh noted that while people know some climate risks, secondary risks like food security and national security are less obvious. gist: Renewed conflict in South Sudan has overwhelmed Juba's military hospital trauma wards.
Political tensions escalated after President Kiir suspended Vice-President Machar over rebel attacks.
Medical staff struggle with severe blood shortages and beds operating at 160% capacity.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Renewed fighting between South Sudan's military and opposition forces has overwhelmed Juba military hospital. The surge in weapon-wounded patients, driven by political conflict and communal violence, has pushed the surgical department to 160% of its bed capacity.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The country's fragile healthcare system is struggling to cope with severe blood shortages and limited resources. Civilians bear the brunt of the violence, which intensified after President Salva Kiir suspended Vice-President Riek Machar following a rebel attack.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: With elections scheduled for December, observers warn that the political crisis and escalating violence risk plunging the country back into a full-scale civil war.

timeline.text: England to host 2031 Netball World Cup

gist: England will host the 2031 Netball World Cup at Manchester's Co-op Live arena.
This marks the fourth time England has been selected to host the tournament.
The event aims to boost the profile and visibility of women's sport.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England has been chosen to host the 2031 Netball World Cup in Manchester. The matches will take place at the Co-op Live indoor arena. This decision was announced by World Netball and England Netball during the national governing body's centenary year. It will be the fourth time the country has hosted the tournament, which was last held in England in 2019 in Liverpool.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Organisers believe the tournament will help increase the visibility and impact of netball and women's sport across the UK. It also offers an opportunity to inspire future players and fans. England's team, the Roses, previously reached the final in 2023 and finished as runners-up in 1975, but they have yet to win the tournament.

timeline.text: Co-op Legal Services using AI to rate workers’ phone calls to customers

gist: Co-op Legal Services is using AI to monitor and rate customer phone calls.
A whistleblower described the automated listening technology as oppressive and dystopian.
The Co-op defended the system as a support tool to improve customer service.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Co-op Legal Services has introduced an OpenAI-trained system to record, analyse and score customer phone calls handled by probate and wills staff. The AI assesses over 50 aspects of each call, providing performance scores to managers.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: A whistleblower called the system "oppressive and dystopian", saying it creates distrust. Trade unions and experts warned that constant AI monitoring risks increasing workplace stress and diminishing sensible practices. However, Co-op Life Services managing director Caoilionn Hurley stated the technology helps ensure high service standards and provides better coaching for staff.

fivew: Co-op Legal Services is using AI to record, analyse and rate employees' phone calls with customers.
The technology was introduced in the last couple of months.
To assess employee performance, boost sales and ensure high standards of customer service.

timeline.text: Covid, Brexit and Liz Truss mini-budget led to lasting decline in mental health, study finds

gist: Major national and global shocks have caused a lasting decline in UK mental health.
The Brexit referendum and the first Covid lockdown caused the most significant psychological distress.
Heightened distress has persisted, leaving NHS mental health services struggling to cope with demand.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A study found that five major shocks since 2016, including Brexit and the first Covid lockdown, caused a lasting decline in UK mental health. Other shocks included the Ukraine invasion, the second lockdown, and Liz Truss's mini-budget.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The research shows that major government decisions and global events seriously damage mental wellbeing. The resulting psychological distress has persisted, contributing to record numbers of people being too sick to work and NHS services struggling to cope with a near-doubling of patients since 2016.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Professor Peter Fonagy is preparing to publish a government-commissioned inquiry report on Friday exploring the rise in mental illness, ADHD, and autism diagnoses.

fivew: Researchers led by Dr Annie Jeffery of University College London.
They found that major systemic shocks caused a lasting decline in UK mental health.
The study was published recently, using data collected between 2009 and 2024.
To estimate the mental health impact of five major systemic shocks.

gist: Rail regulator rejected plans for new train services on the West Coast Main Line.
Proposals by WSMR, Lumo, and Avanti West Coast were denied due to capacity pressures.
Regulator warned additional trains would reduce timetable resilience and increase passenger delays.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Office of Rail and Road rejected plans for new train services linking London with Wrexham, Rochdale, and Blackpool. Applications from Wrexham, Shropshire and Midlands Railway, Lumo, and Avanti West Coast were denied because the line is under significant pressure.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The regulator concluded that adding more services would remove essential gaps in the timetable needed for trains to recover from disruption, risking worse reliability for all passengers.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Campaigners and operators expressed disappointment with the decision, though local representatives stated they would continue fighting for improved rail connectivity.

fivew: The Office of Rail and Road alongside rail operators including WSMR, Lumo, and Avanti West Coast.
Plans for new train services on the West Coast Main Line were rejected.
On the West Coast Main Line connecting locations such as London, Wrexham, Rochdale, and Blackpool.
Due to insufficient capacity and the risk of increasing delays and reducing network reliability.

quotes.text: New services, destinations and greater choice can bring real benefits for passengers and communities.
This is a setback, but it is not the end of our campaign.

gist: Human Rights Watch claims US deportations to third-party African countries are unlawful.
The US government defends these removals as a necessary public safety tool.
Deportees report mistreatment, arbitrary detention and risks of persecution in destination countries.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Human Rights Watch reports that the US has deported over 500 migrants to African countries where they are not citizens. These individuals, who have no prior connection to the destination nations, allegedly face arbitrary detention, ill-treatment, and the risk of being sent back to countries where they fear persecution. Some deportees described being chained during flights and denied basic needs.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The rights group argues these transfers violate international law and are designed to deter migration through suffering. Conversely, the US Department of Homeland Security maintains that third-country removals are essential for public safety and that they receive diplomatic assurances regarding the safety of those removed.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Startup Natura has introduced Interface, a $99 smart ring that allows users to interact with various AI agents through voice commands. The device is designed to help users manage tasks without needing to use a phone. In addition to its AI capabilities, the ring monitors health metrics including heart rate, sleep stages, and activity levels.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The company aims to provide constant access to AI agents by using a wearable form factor. Founder Carlo Edoardo Ferraris suggests the ring could eventually replace many tasks currently performed on screens. While the market features other health-focused rings, Natura claims its device distinguishes itself by combining health tracking with AI communication features.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Pre-orders for the ring are scheduled to open next month, with shipping expected in December or January. While the initial price is $99, the company plans to increase this later. Users will also face a $9 monthly subscription fee following an initial free period.

sections.heading: Why it matters

This is intended to help secure open models, which developers may strip of safeguards, by providing guardrails during inference.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: South Korea announced it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine following a diplomatic dispute. The row began after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that two captured North Korean soldiers had been transferred to Seoul. South Korea stated Ukraine broke an agreement to keep the transfer secret, while Zelensky's office maintained no such non-disclosure agreement existed.

sections.text: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung faced domestic criticism over the revelation, with the opposition accusing him of wanting to cover up the transfer. sections.heading: What happens next

gist: Hackers stole more detailed Asos customer profiles than the company initially disclosed.
Stolen data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and search histories.
Experts warn customers to watch out for convincing phishing scams using this information.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Asos told customers that hackers accessed detailed profiles of potentially millions of users, after BBC News informed the retailer of contact from the cyber criminals. The stolen data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, and website search histories. Hackers, calling themselves Xuanyewen, reportedly gained access by impersonating a trusted contact to obtain an employee's login credentials.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The risk of impersonation scams and convincing phishing attacks has increased. Although Asos stated that no bank details or passwords were stolen, a victim expressed worry that the data could be used for future attacks.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Asos is investigating the breach and will contact customers if further action is needed. Experts advise users to remain highly suspicious of unsolicited messages and to change passwords as a precaution.

gist: The US government has blocked Microsoft and other tech firms from a foreign worker program.
Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of abusing visas to replace American workers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US government has suspended Microsoft and seven other technology firms, including Adobe, from a program that helps foreign workers obtain permanent US residency. Vice President JD Vance accused the companies of abusing the H-1B visa system to replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. The Department of Labor announced it will not process new or pending applications from these firms.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Vance claimed Microsoft laid off American workers while filing thousands of visa applications, undercutting domestic wages. Microsoft rejected these allegations, stating that eighty per cent of its H-1B filings were for existing employees rather than new hires, and that its international staff receive the same compensation as US workers. Immigration advocacy groups argue that attracting global talent benefits the US economy, while Vance described the visa recipients as "indentured servants".

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Microsoft plans to provide the US administration with additional information regarding its hiring practices. Meanwhile, the US government has proposed eliminating the sixty-day grace period for laid-off visa holders.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Let's Encrypt announced it will reduce free certificate lifespans from 90 days down to 64 days, beginning February 10, 2027. Testing for these shorter certificates is scheduled to start on October 14, allowing users to opt in and check their configurations. Furthermore, lifespans are expected to decrease further to 45 days in 2028.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The change aims to encourage administrators to adopt full ACME automation and use ACME Renewal Information rather than relying on manual processes or hardcoded renewal schedules. Shorter validity periods help limit potential damage and vulnerabilities if private keys are stolen or if certificates are misassigned.

gist: El Niño is growing and influences weather globally.
Late winter impacts might include a disrupted polar vortex.
UK snow and ice remain far from guaranteed.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A strong El Niño event is developing in the Pacific Ocean and releasing heat into the atmosphere. This climate phenomenon affects weather patterns worldwide and increases the probability of wet and stormy conditions during the UK autumn. In the late winter period, energy from El Niño can travel upwards to disrupt the polar vortex.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: A disrupted polar vortex can raise the probability of cold weather, ice and snow in the UK. Past winters show mixed evidence as some El Niño years brought extreme cold while others remained very warm, and major cold snaps occurred during different climate phases.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Current forecasts indicate that significant cold weather or snow is not likely in the near future for the UK.

gist: More women report feeling daily anger, driven by unpaid work and everyday sexism.
Cultural media depictions increasingly present female rage as understandable and liberating.
Experts suggest harnessing anger mindfully and authentically rather than suppressing it.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An increasing number of women in the UK and globally are reporting daily anger, breaking away from historical expectations to remain polite and hide frustration. This shift is mirrored in popular culture, where female rage is increasingly depicted as understandable and liberating rather than unstable.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Women continue to shoulder a heavier burden of unpaid work and the mental load compared to men, alongside ongoing threats of violence, sexism, and harassment. While suppressing anger can lead to physical conditions, women expressing anger at work can still face social penalties.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Experts suggest women can harness their anger as a messenger to protect boundaries and confront injustices. Coaches advise using direct language and mindfulness strategies like the RAIN method to channel anger effectively without causing harm.

quotes.text: If someone catcalls me in the street, I rage. I don't care.
We've been brought up with this ridiculous 'good girl' stuff

articles.standfirst: More people in Japan are asking why the nation’s favourite royal, 24-year-old princess Aiko, will never be empress, with a recent poll saying 72% favour a woman emperor

timeline.text: Running out of royals: why calls are growing to let Japan’s princess Aiko take the throne

gist: Calls are growing in Japan to allow Princess Aiko to take the throne.
A 140-year-old law forbids women from ascending to the Chrysanthemum throne.
Conservative government changes safeguard male-only succession despite strong public support for change.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Princess Aiko is the popular only child of Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako. Under a long-standing law, women cannot ascend to the throne. Recent amendments backed by the government of Sanae Takaichi safeguard male-only succession by allowing women to retain royal status after marriage and resurrecting male-line descendants from collateral branches.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The imperial family is shrinking, leaving very few male heirs in the line of succession. Opinion polls show strong public support for a female emperor to avert a looming succession crisis, but conservative leaders insist on maintaining the male-line tradition.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Amendments safeguarding male-only succession go into effect later this month, but public unease and Aiko's popularity may continue to fuel the debate over female emperors.

fivew: Princess Aiko, Emperor Naruhito, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
A looming succession crisis driven by a shrinking royal family clashes with public support for a female emperor.

quotes.text: The unparalleled historic fact that the imperial line has been maintained through the male line for 126 generations is the foundation of the emperor’s authority and legitimacy.

It is important for society to keep progressing ... I believe the duty of the imperial family is to act in response to the requests of society ... I do not think there are any differences between women and men.

gist: An ICE agent shot and injured a man during an enforcement operation in New York.
Reports suggest agents surrounded the man and a five-year-old child in a car.
The shooting sparked angry protests and calls from local officials to end ICE actions.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An ICE agent shot and injured an undocumented Dominican man in the Bronx, New York, on Thursday. Reports indicate agents surrounded the man and a five-year-old child in a car before firing. The child was unharmed. DHS said the officer discharged his weapon during an operation, alleging the man had prior convictions and gang associations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The shooting sparked protests and clashes with police outside the hospital where the man was taken. Local officials condemned the incident, with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani calling it unconscionable and demanding an end to ICE actions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Mayor Mamdani plans to ask US President Donald Trump to end ICE operations in the city. Immigration advocates have called for an independent investigation and the prosecution of the officer.

quotes.text: This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation,
There are more of us than there are of them.

gist: Four Conservative candidates have declared their run for the London mayoral nomination.
The Conservative Party has only won the London mayoralty once in 26 years.
The final shortlist of two candidates is expected to be announced in November.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Four Conservative candidates have declared their bids to run for London mayor in the May 2028 election. The declared runners are Sir James Cleverly, Festus Akinbusoye, Andrew Boff, and Alex Challoner.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Conservatives have only won the London mayoralty once in 26 years, with Boris Johnson. Since then, they have lost three consecutive elections to Labour's Sadiq Khan. However, the party hopes to regain ground following local election victories in Westminster and Wandsworth in May 2026.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The hopefuls must wait until November to see if they make the final shortlist. London party members are expected to choose between the final two candidates, who will likely be announced on 20 November.

sections.text: Eleven individuals were arrested during multiple pro-Palestinian demonstrations across London on Wednesday. gist: Family calls for allergy ratings after a girl died from an unwashed blender.
A cafe and its proprietor were fined following a fatal allergic reaction.
Food safety officials emphasise that businesses must take allergen risks seriously.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A 12-year-old girl died of anaphylactic shock after drinking a milkshake from a south-east London cafe. The blender used had not been washed after making a previous drink containing tree nuts. The cafe and its proprietor were subsequently fined after admitting charges related to food safety.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The family argue that current food hygiene ratings do not inform consumers about a business's allergy management systems. They are campaigning for a dedicated allergy rating scheme so people with food allergies can make safer choices.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Food Standards Agency states it is keeping its policy under review and has produced new guidance and training for businesses regarding allergen responsibilities.

What questions face Pocognoli after Scotland defeat?

gist: Scotland lost two to one against Slovenia at Hampden.
New boss Sebastien Pocognoli faced sharp criticism after the dismal display.
The defeat put Scotland's bid for second place in jeopardy.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Scotland suffered a one-two defeat against Slovenia at Hampden on a dismal night. Slovenia carved out numerous chances, exploiting vast spaces in midfield and at the back. Ryan Christie scored for Scotland, but defensive frailties allowed Aljosa Matko and Danijel Sturm to secure a deserved victory for the visitors.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The damaging defeat threatens Scotland's bid for second place in their Nations League group and a favourable pot two seeding for December's Euros draw. It undermined the recent positivity surrounding the team and brought an abrupt end to manager Sebastien Pocognoli's honeymoon period.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli must nurse his wounds, evaluate his players, and drill his message into the squad. Scotland face their next fixtures in November, playing away against Switzerland and at home against North Macedonia with no real margin for error.

fivew: Scotland's football team managed by Sebastien Pocognoli and Slovenia.
Scotland lost two to one against Slovenia in a Nations League match.
Defensive frailties, a lack of urgency, and tactical exposure allowed Slovenia to dominate.

timeline.text: Eckert free to stay as Southampton boss as Spygate ban suspended

gist: Tonda Eckert avoids a lengthy ban and remains Southampton manager after a suspended sentence.
The FA commission suspended a six-week ban due to Eckert's genuine contrition and mitigation.
Southampton welcomed the decision while owner Dragan Solak criticised the EFL treatment.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Southampton manager Tonda Eckert received a six-week ban from all football, which was suspended until the end of next season, along with a £28,000 fine and reprimand for his role in the Spygate scandal. The FA commission credited him for genuine contrition, avoiding a longer ban that could have cost his job.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The decision allows Eckert to continue leading Southampton as they compete in the Championship this season, putting a regrettable period behind the club according to officials.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The FA has not yet confirmed whether it will appeal the decision, while Southampton prepares to face Portsmouth this weekend.

fivew: Tonda Eckert received a suspended ban and a fine for his role in a spying scandal.
The regulatory commission announced the decision following a hearing.
He was sanctioned for breaches of FA Rule E3.1 relating to spying on training sessions.

quotes.text: We hope this now brings a conclusion to a regrettable period of our history
the way they have treated us is not something we will forget

gist: Liverpool's academy uses strict rules, like car engine limits, to keep young players grounded.
The club is adapting its wage structure to navigate a distorted youth transfer market.
A planned twenty million pound facility revamp aims to boost future player development.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Liverpool's academy director, Alex Inglethorpe, outlined the club's youth development approach, which includes strict rules on phones and car engine sizes to encourage humility.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Brexit and rising competition have distorted the market for 16-year-old players, prompting Liverpool to review its academy wage structure. Additionally, recent departures like Trent Alexander-Arnold and Curtis Jones have left the first team without local-born players.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The club plans a £20 million revamp of its academy facilities by 2028 to continue producing elite talent under new sporting director Julian Ward.

articles.title: Rahm to leave LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms
articles.standfirst: Jon Rahm will leave LIV Golf after deeming the terms for LIV 2.0 "unacceptable", his lawyer has told a bankruptcy court hearing.

timeline.text: Rahm to leave LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms

gist: Jon Rahm is leaving LIV Golf after finding LIV 2.0 terms unacceptable.
LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after losing Saudi funding.
Rahm tops the list of creditors with an unsecured claim of $7.5m.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Jon Rahm is set to leave LIV Golf because he considers the terms of LIV 2.0 unacceptable. LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the United States in September following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabia's funding. The league has secured possible financing from BC Partners Credit for the 2027 season. Rahm and LIV representatives are in advanced discussions for a consensual separation agreement.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rahm is owed an unsecured claim of $7.5m, making him the top creditor among the 30 largest unsecured claims. Participants are owed at least $45m and can leave, as players have no obligation to sign on to LIV 2.0.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Talks are open until 25 October, and it is hoped that a consensual separation agreement will be finalised by a court hearing on 5 November.

gist: Andy Burnham expressed concern if Manchester City owners pulled out.
Reports suggest UAE may halt UK investment over a Premier League ruling.
Sir Richard praised Abu Dhabi's significant and delivered investments in Manchester.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated he would be really concerned if Manchester City owners pulled out. Reports subsequently emerged that the UAE might halt UK-wide investment schemes worth billions due to a Premier League ruling.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Sir Richard highlighted that investment from Abu Dhabi in Manchester and its football club has been very significant, praising their credibility and contributions to the local community.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Sir Richard expressed hope that Manchester does not lose UAE investment, noting he would be concerned if it stopped.

fivew: An ex-Manchester leader defended deals with Manchester City owners amid potential fallout from charges.
Because of concerns over potential fallout from Premier League rulings and investment halts.

gist: JJ Gabriel features in Manchester United's official team photo despite efforts to leave.
Europe's top clubs are interested in the teenager as he holds a European Union passport.
His decision to seek a move was triggered by non-inclusion against Sabah FK.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: JJ Gabriel is included in Manchester United's official team photo for the season. The pictures were taken before he informed the club of his intention to leave. His exit decision was triggered by not being included in the squad to face Sabah FK.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Gabriel is a target for several top European clubs, including Real Madrid and Barcelona. Manchester United hold his registration and would consider legal action if illegal inducement emerges.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Gabriel is set to turn 16 and his next involvement in a United game will virtually certainly be as an opposition player.
